A TOY FOR THE DESIGN, NOT A COMBAT GAME

Invite pressure. Watch the machinery.

Choose Manual progression to open each door and select routes yourself. The other progression modes advance automatically. Click enemy blocks to prioritize them, or select a target policy. Block size follows fuel cost from 50% to 200%; double borders distinguish elites and champions. Press Begin assault. Player controls stay visible beside the inspection tabs. Director, Journal, Lieutenant and Settings change only the inspection panel. Enemies arrive through marked entrances and the Traveler deals abstract damage automatically. Supports absorb fire first; clicks and target policies choose among eligible targets. Burst strategy changes timing, not targeting.

  1. Move through four chambers per zone. Zone activation introduces its entire 100-point budget. First room entry requests a portion of the zone’s Potential, capped by what remains. The baseline requests 25 points at depth 1; it never tops up an expensive prepared group. Re-entry repeats nothing.
  2. Automatic spill damage. A pulse fires every 0.5s. Excess damage carries to the lowest-HP eligible enemy; beams show each hit. Enemy health and incoming damage scale with point cost. DPS charges refill at one per 10s up to the selected capacity. With two or more charges, use one immediately on arrival. A lone charge is always used when another is within two seconds of recharging. Otherwise, Last-charge strategy chooses its trigger: 50% health, 20+ living fuel-equivalent, or a living support/glass cannon. A charged pulse deals 4× passive damage. Health regenerates at the selected base rate with enemies present and five times that rate while the battlefield is empty. The 50% health trigger is retained across potion healing until the next pulse. Potions automatically restore 40 HP below 50% health. Every 30 fuel worth of kills restores one missing potion; defeating any scripted leader refills all potion slots. No recharge progress banks while full. Change player stats offers stepped capacities, maximum health, damage and regeneration. Changes stay pending until Apply & restart; Restore baseline stages the default values. The optional chest remains visible under Enter Sanctum. There are no manual attack or recovery buttons.
  3. Select your approach. Slow and steady clears every living enemy, then requires either 70% health with two charges, or full health with one charge. Press forward advances immediately when all enemies are cleared, regardless of health or charges. Both clearing approaches stay in the current room when a new wave has already been telegraphed. Charge ahead breaks crystals early. The simulated player spends automatic burst charges when pressure builds. Stop advancing suspends automatic movement while combat, fuel flow and recovery continue. Pause stops the whole simulation. Reset run restarts the current activity paused, retaining preferences and banked Keystones. Route choice controls whether automatic movement visits optional wings.
  4. Finite zone fuel. Passive Potential-to-Available flow is 0.5 points/sec; funding determines arrival timing. A one-second engine recovery lockout protects spawning work. The selected door blinks up to six seconds before passive funding completes; its enemies emerge from that same door. Player-funded arrivals skip the warning. Entering rooms accelerates release; it adds no fuel. Waiting can exhaust the whole activated zone before later rooms are visited. Those rooms do not manufacture replacement waves.
  5. Tagged portals. The zone offers forward, behind, open-side and sealed-side portals. The Director chooses a legal portal using its profile preferences; Champion cores prefer sealed-side entrances. The zone stages the selected units at that location. Sealed side doors are offered as breach opportunities. A breach card chooses an authored standalone group (about 8–10 points at depth 1) without padding; it arrives without warning and opens that seal. Later arrivals use the open door normally.
  6. Prepared groups persist. Normal menu changes preserve N+1. Affordable groups arrive as soon as assets, engine recovery and a safe entrance permit. Warnings add no delay after affordability.
  7. Final group budgeting. Composition is capped by Available plus Potential. If its remaining tail cannot fund the cheapest eligible group, expandable groups absorb what fits and half the added cost transfers immediately. Standalone breaches stay small. Hard limits remain; unspendable residue is recorded. Boss arrivals never flush fuel or cancel a prepared group.
  8. Progression and rewards. Lieutenants arrive 10 seconds after entering the final chamber with opposition, or after a 6-second zone-completion timer in any chamber. Completion requires no living mobs and no further scheduled or fundable groups. Completion during the long timer subtracts 4 seconds from its deadline, possibly causing immediate arrival. Their defeat and exhausted zone budget permit exit, even with defenders alive. The first lieutenant yields one Keystone, the fourth another, and the final boss one. Return after final victory and zone spending to bank them. Five banked Keystones and a final-boss clear unlock the separate Sanctum.

Zone budgets, room releases and tagged portal preferences implement the clarified design. Normal wave targets are 15–40 points at depth 1, most balanced waves 18–25; final cleanup may be smaller. The review supersedes the pitch’s earlier per-encounter budgets and fragment estimate. No Labyrinth cache economy is included. Floor bosses have 20 fuel-equivalent, 550 HP and 3.84 DPS at baseline but consume zero Director fuel; linked guardians retain 4 fuel-equivalent. Scripted lieutenants, Guardians and bosses are visible activity actors with health; their staging, approach thresholds and exit permissions and the exact termination button are toy authoring decisions. This toy treats scripted actor survival as opposition for the quiet milestone. Finished remains a historical observation and never controls movement. Spatial safety, load readiness and attacks are abstracted.

Encounter selection supports ordered lists and seeded random draws without replacement. Cards incompatible with current portal/group opportunities are filtered. Reshuffle cards permit early repeats. Personality list progress persists through rooms; prepared groups survive ordinary mode/personality changes. Terminal residue uses affordable cleanup only when no listed composition fits the total remaining budget.

The Journal summarizes each uninterrupted combat when the last living enemy dies. Overlapping arrivals belong to that same fight. Copy log shares the concise journal; Export full run retains the detailed event trace and health timeline.

Try these experiments

Run Heavy, then switch menus while N+1 waits. Block an entrance during its warning. Breach while enemies survive. Wait until several volumes finish together, then enter another zone and watch the residue fund the preserved plan.
